claims.text: The pristine (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
The pristine alloy has poor mechanical integrity and tends to crack under mechanical loading.
Approximately 3–5 vol% fine, ductile Cu nanoparticles can be incorporated to form an in situ composite.
The added Cu nanoparticles will preferentially locate at grain boundaries and within grains.
The Cu nanoparticles will arrest crack propagation.
The Cu nanoparticles will improve load transfer.
The ductile Cu phase will blunt crack tips.
The ductile Cu phase will alleviate stress concentrations.
Adding 3–5 vol% Cu will maintain the phase transition responsible for the caloric response.
Adding Cu nanoparticles will significantly increase the alloy's mechanical robustness.
The modified alloy will achieve compressive strength nearer to or exceeding 150–200 MPa.
The modified alloy's caloric response will remain within 10% of that of the pristine alloy.
The expected improvement is limited to magnetic-field, pressure-field, temperature, and mechanical-loading regimes similar to those previously used for the pristine alloy.
Performance may differ outside the stated testing regimes.
Small variations in Cu content or distribution could reduce the caloric response more than anticipated.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome allows strength 'nearer to or exceeding 150–200 MPa,' whereas the falsification rule can be read as requiring strength greater than 150–200 MPa. A result within or near that range could therefore satisfy the prediction while failing the stated test.
